---- MODULE W4Od12m2p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Instances, Controllers, Slots

Unowned == "unowned"
Quorum == Cardinality(Controllers)

VARIABLES phase, journal, tally, held, owner

vars == <<phase, journal, tally, held, owner>>

Round == [ins : Instances, slot : Slots]
Journals == UNION { [1 .. n -> Round] : n \in 0 .. Cardinality(Instances) }
Cur == journal[1]

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Instances -> {"idle", "preparing"}]
    /\ journal \in Journals
    /\ tally \in 0 .. Quorum
    /\ held \in [Instances -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Instances \cup {Unowned}]

Init ==
    /\ phase = [i \in Instances |-> "idle"]
    /\ journal = << >>
    /\ tally = 0
    /\ held = [i \in Instances |-> {}]
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Unowned]

Begin(i, s) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "idle"
    /\ owner[s] = Unowned
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "preparing"]
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, [ins |-> i, slot |-> s])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, held, owner>>

CollectVote ==
    /\ journal # << >>
    /\ tally < Quorum
    /\ tally' = tally + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, journal, held, owner>>

RefuseHead ==
    /\ journal # << >>
    /\ tally < Quorum
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![Cur.ins] = "idle"]
    /\ journal' = Tail(journal)
    /\ tally' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, owner>>

CommitHead ==
    /\ journal # << >>
    /\ tally = Quorum
    /\ owner[Cur.slot] = Unowned
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![Cur.slot] = Cur.ins]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![Cur.ins] = held[Cur.ins] \cup {Cur.slot}]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![Cur.ins] = "idle"]
    /\ journal' = Tail(journal)
    /\ tally' = 0

AbortStaleHead ==
    /\ journal # << >>
    /\ tally = Quorum
    /\ owner[Cur.slot] # Unowned
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![Cur.ins] = "idle"]
    /\ journal' = Tail(journal)
    /\ tally' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, owner>>

Release(i, s) ==
    /\ s \in held[i]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![i] = held[i] \ {s}]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Unowned]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, journal, tally>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Slots : Begin(i, s) \/ Release(i, s)
    \/ CollectVote \/ RefuseHead \/ CommitHead \/ AbortStaleHead

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(CollectVote)
    /\ WF_vars(CommitHead \/ AbortStaleHead)

OwnedSlotsAppearInTheirOwnersHeldSet ==
    \A s \in Slots : (owner[s] # Unowned) => (s \in held[owner[s]])

EveryRoundSettles ==
    \A i \in Instances : (phase[i] = "preparing") ~> (phase[i] = "idle")
====
nl:
A regional blood-bank inventory tracker manages one shared pool of refrigerated storage slots. Two independent tracking instances run against that single pool. Neither instance can see the other's internal state; they interact only through the pool and through the pool's serialized commit journal, a first-in-first-out queue of reservation rounds waiting to be resolved by the participating fridge controllers under two-phase commit.

The system behaves as follows. An idle instance may Begin a reservation by choosing a storage slot that looks unowned at that moment, entering its preparing phase and appending a round record naming itself and the chosen slot to the tail of the commit journal. Only the round at the head of the journal is actively being voted on. While that head round is short of a full set of votes, the CollectVote step records one more fridge controller's yes vote for it. Alternatively RefuseHead may fire while the head round is still short of a full set of votes: a controller declines, the round is discarded from the journal, its vote tally resets and the owning instance returns to idle. Once the head round has collected a vote from every controller, it resolves in one of two ways. CommitHead applies when the pool still shows the round's slot as unowned: the pool records the round's instance as the slot's owner, that instance adds the slot to its own set of held slots, the round leaves the journal, the tally resets and the instance returns to idle. AbortStaleHead applies when the pool instead shows the slot already owned, because the other instance won the race while this round was collecting votes: the round is discarded with no change to the pool, the tally resets and the instance returns to idle. Finally, an instance may Release a slot it holds, which removes the slot from its held set and marks the slot unowned in the pool in the same step.

The hazard is that both instances can have live rounds for the very same slot, since Begin only inspects the pool at the instant it fires and the pool can change while a round waits in the journal. Correctness rests entirely on the commit-time re-check and on Release updating local bookkeeping and the shared pool together.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot that the shared pool records as owned appears in the held set of the very instance the pool names as its owner.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every instance that enters its preparing phase eventually returns to idle.

---- MODULE W4Od19m9p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Branches, Slots, MaxEpoch

NoBranch == "nobranch"

VARIABLES epoch, config, known, registry, placed

vars == <<epoch, config, known, registry, placed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ config \subseteq Branches
    /\ known \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ registry \in [Slots -> Branches \cup {NoBranch}]
    /\ placed \in [Branches -> SUBSET Slots]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ config = Branches
    /\ known = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ registry = [s \in Slots |-> NoBranch]
    /\ placed = [b \in Branches |-> {}]

Reserve(b, s) ==
    /\ b \in config
    /\ known[b] = epoch
    /\ registry[s] = NoBranch
    /\ registry' = [registry EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![b] = placed[b] \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, known>>

Return(b, s) ==
    /\ s \in placed[b]
    /\ registry[s] = b
    /\ registry' = [registry EXCEPT ![s] = NoBranch]
    /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![b] = placed[b] \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, known>>

CatchUp(b) ==
    /\ known[b] < epoch
    /\ known' = [known EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, registry, placed>>

Reconfigure(b) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ b \in config
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ config' = config \ {b}
    /\ registry' = [s \in Slots |-> IF registry[s] = b THEN NoBranch ELSE registry[s]]
    /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED known

Rejoin(b) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ b \notin config
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ config' = config \cup {b}
    /\ known' = [known EXCEPT ![b] = epoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<registry, placed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Branches, s \in Slots : Reserve(b, s) \/ Return(b, s)
    \/ \E b \in Branches : CatchUp(b) \/ Reconfigure(b) \/ Rejoin(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PlacedHoldsAreAttributedToTheirBranch ==
    \A b \in Branches, s \in Slots : (s \in placed[b]) => (registry[s] = b)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Branches = {b1, b2}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PlacedHoldsAreAttributedToTheirBranch
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A county library book reservation system spreads reservation authority across branch libraries. Each physical copy of a title has a numbered hold slot, and any branch may place a patron's hold into a slot. Because branches come and go from the cooperative, the system uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a single configuration epoch counter advances every time a branch joins or leaves, and a branch may only place holds while the epoch it knows about matches the current epoch. A branch can be slow without being failed, so a branch that has fallen behind is still running and still receiving requests; it simply has an out-of-date epoch number until it catches up.

The system behaves as follows. Reserve places a hold: an active branch whose known epoch equals the current epoch may take a slot that the shared registry shows as unclaimed, writing itself into the registry for that slot and adding the slot to its own list of placed holds. Return releases a hold: a branch that has a slot in its own list, and that the registry also attributes to it, clears the registry entry and drops the slot from its list. CatchUp models the slow branch: a branch whose known epoch is behind the current epoch advances its known epoch to the current value, after which it may act again. Reconfigure removes an active branch from the cooperative: the epoch counter advances, the branch leaves the configuration, and every hold it was holding is revoked from both its own list and the shared registry in the same step. Rejoin admits a branch that is not currently in the configuration: the epoch counter advances, the branch enters the configuration, and it starts out knowing the new epoch.

The hazard is that a branch which has fallen behind, or one that has been dropped from the configuration entirely, may still try to place holds on slots it believes are free, which is exactly how the same slot ends up allocated twice. The epoch match required by Reserve, together with the revocation performed by Reconfigure, is what stands between the cooperative and a double-booked copy.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot that a branch lists among its own placed holds is attributed to that same branch by the shared registry.

---- MODULE W4Od8m2p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Seats, Approvers, MaxOverrides

Empty == "empty"

VARIABLES txn, consents, chart, roster, budget

vars == <<txn, consents, chart, roster, budget>>

Txns == [stu : Students, seat : Seats]
Cur == CHOOSE r \in txn : TRUE

TypeOK ==
    /\ txn \subseteq Txns
    /\ Cardinality(txn) <= 1
    /\ consents \subseteq Approvers
    /\ chart \in [Seats -> Students \cup {Empty}]
    /\ roster \in [Students -> SUBSET Seats]
    /\ budget \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ txn = {}
    /\ consents = {}
    /\ chart = [se \in Seats |-> Empty]
    /\ roster = [st \in Students |-> {}]
    /\ budget = MaxOverrides

Open(st, se) ==
    /\ txn = {}
    /\ chart[se] = Empty
    /\ txn' = {[stu |-> st, seat |-> se]}
    /\ consents' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, roster, budget>>

Approve(a) ==
    /\ txn # {}
    /\ a \notin consents
    /\ consents' = consents \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, chart, roster, budget>>

Reject(a) ==
    /\ txn # {}
    /\ a \notin consents
    /\ txn' = {}
    /\ consents' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chart, roster, budget>>

Seat(st, se) ==
    /\ chart' = [chart EXCEPT ![se] = st]
    /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![st] = roster[st] \cup {se}]

Commit ==
    /\ txn # {}
    /\ consents = Approvers
    /\ chart[Cur.seat] = Empty
    /\ Seat(Cur.stu, Cur.seat)
    /\ txn' = {}
    /\ consents' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED budget

AdminOverride ==
    /\ txn # {}
    /\ budget > 0
    /\ chart[Cur.seat] = Empty
    /\ Seat(Cur.stu, Cur.seat)
    /\ budget' = budget - 1
    /\ txn' = {}
    /\ consents' = {}

Drop(st, se) ==
    /\ se \in roster[st]
    /\ chart[se] = st
    /\ chart' = [chart EXCEPT ![se] = Empty]
    /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![st] = roster[st] \ {se}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, consents, budget>>

ApproveSome == \E a \in Approvers : Approve(a)

Next ==
    \/ \E st \in Students, se \in Seats : Open(st, se) \/ Drop(st, se)
    \/ \E a \in Approvers : Approve(a) \/ Reject(a)
    \/ Commit
    \/ AdminOverride

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(ApproveSome)
    /\ WF_vars(Commit)

RosteredSeatsMatchTheChart ==
    \A st \in Students, se \in Seats : (se \in roster[st]) => (chart[se] = st)

EveryTransactionCloses == (txn # {}) ~> (txn = {})
====
nl:
A university course-registration system seats students into individual numbered seats of a course section. Seating is not done unilaterally: the registrar opens a registration transaction and runs a two-phase commit across the departmental approvers, and only one transaction is open at a time. A privileged administrator override exists for exceptional cases, and the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. Open starts a transaction: with no transaction currently open, the registrar picks a student and a seat that the seating chart shows as empty, records the pair as the open transaction and clears the approval set. Approve records one departmental approver's consent for the open transaction; an approver who has already consented cannot consent twice. Reject models an approver refusing: while a transaction is open, an approver who has not yet consented may kill it outright, which discards the transaction and clears the approval set without touching the seating chart or any roster. Commit completes the normal path: when every approver has consented and the seat is still empty on the chart, the chart records the student in that seat, the seat is added to the student's roster, the transaction closes and the approval set clears. AdminOverride is the exceptional path: while a transaction is open, the seat is still empty and override budget remains, the administrator seats the student immediately without waiting for the approvers, consuming one unit of override budget, updating chart and roster together and closing the transaction. Drop removes a seating: a student who has a seat on their roster gives it up, clearing the chart entry and the roster entry in the same step.

The hazard the design guards against is the same seat being handed to two students, which would happen if the roster and the seating chart were ever allowed to disagree — in particular if the override path updated one without the other, or if a commit landed on a seat that had already been filled.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every seat that appears on some student's roster is recorded on the seating chart as belonging to that same student.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every registration transaction that is opened eventually closes.

---- MODULE W4Od12m8p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Fridges, ShelfIds, Techs, MaxCap

NoTech == "notech"
Shelves == Fridges \X ShelfIds

VARIABLES coarse, fine, capacity, roster

vars == <<coarse, fine, capacity, roster>>

LockedIn(f) == {sh \in Shelves : sh[1] = f /\ fine[sh] # NoTech}

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Fridges -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ fine \in [Shelves -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ capacity \in [Fridges -> 0 .. MaxCap]
    /\ roster \subseteq Techs

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [f \in Fridges |-> NoTech]
    /\ fine = [sh \in Shelves |-> NoTech]
    /\ capacity = [f \in Fridges |-> MaxCap]
    /\ roster = Techs

AcquireCoarse(t, f) ==
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ coarse[f] = NoTech
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![f] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, capacity, roster>>

AcquireFine(t, sh) ==
    /\ coarse[sh[1]] = t
    /\ fine[sh] = NoTech
    /\ Cardinality(LockedIn(sh[1])) < capacity[sh[1]]
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![sh] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, capacity, roster>>

ReleaseFine(t, sh) ==
    /\ fine[sh] = t
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![sh] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, capacity, roster>>

ReleaseCoarse(t, f) ==
    /\ coarse[f] = t
    /\ \A sh \in LockedIn(f) : fine[sh] # t
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![f] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, capacity, roster>>

Resize(t, f, n) ==
    /\ coarse[f] = t
    /\ n >= Cardinality(LockedIn(f))
    /\ capacity' = [capacity EXCEPT ![f] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, roster>>

Revoke(t) ==
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ roster' = roster \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, capacity>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs, f \in Fridges : AcquireCoarse(t, f) \/ ReleaseCoarse(t, f)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, sh \in Shelves : AcquireFine(t, sh) \/ ReleaseFine(t, sh)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, f \in Fridges, n \in 0 .. MaxCap : Resize(t, f, n)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Revoke(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FineLocksRestOnTheirFridgeLock ==
    \A sh \in Shelves : (fine[sh] # NoTech) => (coarse[sh[1]] = fine[sh])
====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker protects its cold storage with a two-level lock hierarchy. Each walk-in fridge carries one coarse lock, and every shelf inside a fridge carries its own fine lock. A technician must be holding the coarse lock on a fridge before touching any shelf lock inside it. Each fridge also has a shelf-occupancy capacity that can be changed at runtime as trays are reconfigured, and the roster of authorized technicians can shrink while the system is running.

The system behaves as follows. AcquireCoarse lets a technician who is currently on the authorized roster take the coarse lock of a fridge that nobody holds. AcquireFine lets a technician who already holds the coarse lock of a fridge take the free fine lock of one of that fridge's shelves, provided the fridge is not already at its current shelf capacity. ReleaseFine gives back a fine lock the technician holds. ReleaseCoarse gives back a coarse lock the technician holds, but only once that technician holds no fine lock inside that fridge. Resize changes a fridge's shelf capacity: the technician holding the fridge's coarse lock sets a new capacity, which may not be smaller than the number of shelves in that fridge already locked. Revoke removes a technician from the authorized roster without disturbing any lock that technician is currently holding, which is how a technician becomes stale while still apparently in control of storage.

The dangerous case is a technician acting on a shelf inside a fridge whose coarse lock it does not hold — either because it never took it, or because it took the fine lock and the coarse lock ended up elsewhere. Note that authorization is checked only when the coarse lock is taken, so a revoked technician may still be holding locks; what must never happen is a shelf lock floating free of the matching fridge lock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a technician holds the fine lock of a shelf, that same technician holds the coarse lock of the fridge that shelf belongs to.

---- MODULE W4Od4m6p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Bays, Capacity, MaxTTL

Idle == "idle"

VARIABLES onLine, bayOf, ttl, broken, washed

vars == <<onLine, bayOf, ttl, broken, washed>>

InSomeBay(c) == \E b \in Bays : bayOf[b] = c
Expired == {b \in Bays : bayOf[b] # Idle /\ ttl[b] = 0}

TypeOK ==
    /\ onLine \subseteq Cars
    /\ bayOf \in [Bays -> Cars \cup {Idle}]
    /\ ttl \in [Bays -> 0 .. MaxTTL]
    /\ broken \subseteq Bays
    /\ washed \subseteq Cars

Init ==
    /\ onLine = {}
    /\ bayOf = [b \in Bays |-> Idle]
    /\ ttl = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ broken = {}
    /\ washed = {}

Admit(c) ==
    /\ c \notin onLine
    /\ c \notin washed
    /\ Cardinality(onLine) < Capacity
    /\ onLine' = onLine \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayOf, ttl, broken, washed>>

Lease(b, c) ==
    /\ bayOf[b] = Idle
    /\ c \in onLine
    /\ ~InSomeBay(c)
    /\ bayOf' = [bayOf EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![b] = MaxTTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, broken, washed>>

Finish(b) ==
    /\ bayOf[b] # Idle
    /\ b \notin broken
    /\ washed' = washed \cup {bayOf[b]}
    /\ onLine' = onLine \ {bayOf[b]}
    /\ bayOf' = [bayOf EXCEPT ![b] = Idle]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED broken

Tick ==
    /\ \E b \in Bays : ttl[b] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [b \in Bays |-> IF ttl[b] > 0 THEN ttl[b] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, bayOf, broken, washed>>

ReclaimExpired ==
    /\ Expired # {}
    /\ bayOf' = [b \in Bays |-> IF b \in Expired THEN Idle ELSE bayOf[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, ttl, broken, washed>>

Crash(b) ==
    /\ b \notin broken
    /\ broken' = broken \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, bayOf, ttl, washed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Admit(c)
    \/ \E b \in Bays, c \in Cars : Lease(b, c)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Finish(b) \/ Crash(b)
    \/ Tick
    \/ ReclaimExpired

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Tick)
    /\ WF_vars(ReclaimExpired)

ConveyorStaysWithinCapacity == Cardinality(onLine) <= Capacity

EveryBayFreesItsCar == \A b \in Bays : (bayOf[b] # Idle) ~> (bayOf[b] = Idle)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
    Bays = {b1, b2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxTTL = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ConveyorStaysWithinCapacity
PROPERTY EveryBayFreesItsCar
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line pulls cars through a fixed number of washing bays. The line itself has a hard capacity: only so many cars may be on the conveyor at once. Bay assignment is done with leases rather than permanent ownership, because a bay's washer unit can crash silently — it stops doing any work and gives no notice at all — and the line must not be blocked forever by a car parked in a dead bay. Every lease therefore carries a countdown, and an expired lease is reclaimed whether or not the bay ever finished the car.

The system behaves as follows. Admit puts a new car onto the conveyor, and may only fire while the number of cars already on the line is below the line capacity; a car that has already been washed is never re-admitted. Lease hands an idle bay a car that is on the line and not already sitting in some bay, and starts that lease's countdown at its full value. Finish is the happy path: a bay whose washer has not crashed completes the car it holds, removing the car from the conveyor, marking it washed, and returning the bay to idle with a zero countdown. Tick advances time for the whole line at once, decrementing every lease countdown that is still above zero. ReclaimExpired fires whenever at least one occupied bay has run its countdown to zero, and in a single step it empties every such bay back to idle; the cars in those bays stay on the conveyor and must be leased a bay again. Crash marks a bay's washer as silently broken, after which that bay can never finish a car again, though it can still be leased and reclaimed.

The line's hard capacity is the thing that must hold no matter how many bays crash, how many leases expire, or how many cars get recycled back onto the conveyor by a reclaim.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars on the conveyor never exceeds the line capacity.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bay that is holding a car eventually returns to idle.

---- MODULE W4Od8m6p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxTTL

Free == "free"

VARIABLES holder, ttl, inside, crashed

vars == <<holder, ttl, inside, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Nodes \cup {Free}
    /\ ttl \in 0 .. MaxTTL
    /\ inside \subseteq Nodes
    /\ crashed \subseteq Nodes

Init ==
    /\ holder = Free
    /\ ttl = 0
    /\ inside = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Grant(n) ==
    /\ holder = Free
    /\ holder' = n
    /\ ttl' = MaxTTL
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inside, crashed>>

Enter(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ n \notin inside
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ inside' = inside \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ttl, crashed>>

Exit(n) ==
    /\ n \in inside
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ inside' = inside \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ttl, crashed>>

Renew(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ ttl' = MaxTTL
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inside, crashed>>

Tick ==
    /\ ttl > 0
    /\ ttl' = ttl - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inside, crashed>>

Expire ==
    /\ holder # Free
    /\ ttl = 0
    /\ holder' = Free
    /\ inside' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, crashed>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ttl, inside>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Grant(n) \/ Enter(n) \/ Exit(n) \/ Renew(n) \/ Crash(n)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Expire

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OccupantOfEditorHoldsTheLease ==
    \A n \in inside : holder = n
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    MaxTTL = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OccupantOfEditorHoldsTheLease
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A university course-registration system lets several registration nodes edit the live catalog, but the catalog editor is a critical resource that exactly one node may be inside at any moment. Access is granted as a lease with a countdown rather than as a permanent grant, because a registration node can crash silently: it stops responding without any notice, and if it happens to be inside the editor at that moment nothing it does will ever bring it back out.

The system behaves as follows. Grant hands the lease to a node when the lease is free, starting that node's countdown at its full value. Enter lets the node that currently holds an unexpired lease step into the catalog editor, provided it has not already done so and has not crashed. Exit lets a node that is inside the editor and has not crashed step back out; the lease itself stays with that node. Renew lets an uncrashed lease holder whose countdown has not yet run out reset the countdown to its full value, which is how a healthy node keeps working. Tick advances the clock, decrementing the countdown whenever it is above zero. Expire fires once the countdown has reached zero while the lease is still held: the lease is released and, crucially, anyone still inside the editor is forcibly evicted in the same step, because the whole point of the countdown is to recover from a holder that will never come out on its own. Crash marks a node as silently failed, after which that node can no longer enter, exit or renew anything.

The dangerous scenario is a node lingering inside the editor after the lease has moved on — either because expiry released the lease without evicting the occupant, or because a second node was let in while the first was still inside.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any node inside the catalog editor is the node that currently holds the lease.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m9p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, Vouchers, MaxEpoch, MaxCap

NoMachine == "nomachine"

VARIABLES epoch, known, dispenser, audit, capacity

vars == <<epoch, known, dispenser, audit, capacity>>

Honoured == {v \in Vouchers : dispenser[v] # NoMachine}

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ known \in [Machines -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ dispenser \in [Vouchers -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]
    /\ audit \subseteq (Vouchers \X Machines \X (0 .. MaxEpoch))
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ known = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ dispenser = [v \in Vouchers |-> NoMachine]
    /\ audit = {}
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

Reconfigure(n) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ capacity' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<known, dispenser, audit>>

SyncAll ==
    /\ \E m \in Machines : known[m] < epoch
    /\ known' = [m \in Machines |-> epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, dispenser, audit, capacity>>

Dispense(m, v) ==
    /\ known[m] = epoch
    /\ dispenser[v] = NoMachine
    /\ Cardinality(Honoured) < capacity
    /\ dispenser' = [dispenser EXCEPT ![v] = m]
    /\ audit' = audit \cup {<<v, m, epoch>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, known, capacity>>

Replay(m, v) ==
    /\ dispenser[v] = m
    /\ <<v, m, epoch>> \notin audit
    /\ audit' = audit \cup {<<v, m, epoch>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, known, dispenser, capacity>>

Reset(m) ==
    /\ known[m] > 0
    /\ known' = [known EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, dispenser, audit, capacity>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in 0 .. MaxCap : Reconfigure(n)
    \/ SyncAll
    \/ \E m \in Machines, v \in Vouchers : Dispense(m, v) \/ Replay(m, v)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Reset(m)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(SyncAll)

AuditEntriesAgreeWithTheRecord ==
    \A e \in audit : dispenser[e[1]] = e[2]

StaleMachinesCatchUp ==
    \A m \in Machines : (known[m] < epoch) ~> (known[m] = epoch)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2}
    Vouchers = {v1, v2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxCap = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AuditEntriesAgreeWithTheRecord
PROPERTY StaleMachinesCatchUp
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A network of vending machines runs a promotional voucher campaign. Redeeming a voucher is irreversible: the machine drops the item and there is no way to put it back, so a voucher must be dispensed against at most once across the whole network. The fleet is coordinated by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. A single campaign epoch counter is bumped whenever headquarters changes the campaign, and each change also resets how many vouchers the campaign will honour in total, so the campaign capacity varies at runtime. A machine may only dispense while the epoch it knows matches the current campaign epoch. Alongside the authoritative record of which machine dispensed each voucher, the network keeps an append-only audit log of dispense events, each stamped with the epoch in force when it was written.

The system behaves as follows. Reconfigure bumps the campaign epoch and simultaneously sets a new campaign capacity, which may be larger or smaller than before. SyncAll is the headquarters broadcast: whenever at least one machine is behind, every machine in the fleet is brought up to the current epoch in one step. Dispense is the irreversible act: a machine whose known epoch matches the campaign epoch, faced with a voucher that the authoritative record shows as never dispensed, and with the number of already-dispensed vouchers still below the campaign capacity, records itself against that voucher and writes an audit entry naming the voucher, itself, and the current epoch. Replay covers duplicate customer requests: a machine that the record already shows as the dispenser of a voucher may write a fresh audit entry for it at the current epoch without dropping a second item. Reset models a machine rebooting and losing its campaign state, dropping its known epoch back to zero so that it is stale until the next broadcast.

The failure this design must exclude is a second, different machine dispensing against a voucher that has already been honoured, which would show up as an audit entry attributing the voucher to a machine other than the one on record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the audit log names the very machine that the authoritative record shows as the dispenser of that entry's voucher.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every machine that has fallen behind the campaign epoch eventually knows the current epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od13m5p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, Adjustments, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, seen, round, votes, settled

vars == <<version, seen, round, votes, settled>>

Rounds == [base : 0 .. MaxVersion, by : Machines, adj : Adjustments]
Open == CHOOSE r \in round : TRUE
Majority == Cardinality(Machines) \div 2 + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
    /\ seen \in [Machines -> 0 .. MaxVersion]
    /\ round \subseteq Rounds
    /\ Cardinality(round) <= 1
    /\ votes \subseteq Machines
    /\ settled \subseteq ((0 .. MaxVersion) \X Adjustments)

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ seen = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ round = {}
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ settled = {}

Read(m) ==
    /\ seen[m] # version
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![m] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, round, votes, settled>>

Propose(m, a) ==
    /\ round = {}
    /\ round' = {[base |-> seen[m], by |-> m, adj |-> a]}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, seen, settled>>

Vote(m) ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ m \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, seen, round, settled>>

CommitUpdate ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Majority
    /\ Open.base = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ settled' = settled \cup {<<version, Open.adj>>}
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED seen

AbortStaleRound ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Majority
    /\ Open.base # version
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, seen, settled>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Read(m) \/ Vote(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines, a \in Adjustments : Propose(m, a)
    \/ CommitUpdate
    \/ AbortStaleRound

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SupersededVersionsFormAnUnbrokenChain ==
    {e[1] : e \in settled} = 0 .. version - 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
    Adjustments = {1, 2}
    MaxVersion = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SupersededVersionsFormAnUnbrokenChain
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A network of vending machines shares one pricing record. Any machine may propose a change to it, but a change only takes effect once a quorum of machines has voted for it. Machines can be slow without being failed: a slow machine is still running and still able to propose, it simply read the pricing record a while ago and may be working from a version number that has since moved on. Alongside the record the network keeps a settlement log: one entry per accepted change, recording which record version that change was computed against and the adjustment it applied.

The system behaves as follows. Read refreshes one machine's view, setting the version it believes current to the record's actual current version. Propose opens a change round when no round is open: the proposing machine names the version it last read as the base of its change, names the adjustment it wants, and the vote set starts empty. Vote records one machine's support for the open round; no machine votes twice in a round. CommitUpdate closes the round successfully when a strict majority of machines has voted and the round's base version is still the record's current version: the version counter advances by one and a settlement log entry is written recording the base version that was superseded and the adjustment applied. AbortStaleRound closes the round unsuccessfully when a strict majority has voted but the record has moved on since the round's base was read; the round is thrown away, nothing is logged and the version counter does not move.

The danger is a lost update: a change computed against an old version quietly overwriting a change that landed in between, which would leave a gap or a duplicate in the chain of superseded versions recorded by the settlement log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The versions recorded as superseded in the settlement log are exactly the versions from zero up to one below the record's current version, with no gaps and no repeats.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Capacity, MaxGen, MaxCleared

VARIABLES queue, mandate, gen, accredited, cleared

vars == <<queue, mandate, gen, accredited, cleared>>

Instructions == [bank : Banks, stamp : 0 .. MaxGen]
Queues == UNION { [1 .. n -> Instructions] : n \in 0 .. Capacity }

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Queues
    /\ mandate \in 0 .. MaxGen
    /\ gen \in [Banks -> 0 .. MaxGen]
    /\ accredited \subseteq Banks
    /\ cleared \in 0 .. MaxCleared

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ mandate = 0
    /\ gen = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ accredited = Banks
    /\ cleared = 0

Submit(b) ==
    /\ b \in accredited
    /\ gen[b] = mandate
    /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [bank |-> b, stamp |-> mandate])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mandate, gen, accredited, cleared>>

SettleHead ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ cleared' = IF cleared < MaxCleared THEN cleared + 1 ELSE cleared
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mandate, gen, accredited>>

RotateMandate ==
    /\ mandate < MaxGen
    /\ mandate' = mandate + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, gen, accredited, cleared>>

Sync(b) ==
    /\ gen[b] < mandate
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![b] = mandate]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, mandate, accredited, cleared>>

Revoke(b) ==
    /\ b \in accredited
    /\ accredited' = accredited \ {b}
    /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA e : e.bank # b)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mandate, gen, cleared>>

Accredit(b) ==
    /\ b \notin accredited
    /\ accredited' = accredited \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, mandate, gen, cleared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Submit(b) \/ Sync(b) \/ Revoke(b) \/ Accredit(b)
    \/ SettleHead
    \/ RotateMandate

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(SettleHead)

QueuedWorkBelongsToAccreditedBanks ==
    \A n \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[n].bank \in accredited

BackpressureAlwaysRelaxes == (Len(queue) = Capacity) ~> (Len(queue) < Capacity)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxGen = 1
    MaxCleared = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT QueuedWorkBelongsToAccreditedBanks
PROPERTY BackpressureAlwaysRelaxes
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch accepts payment instructions from member banks into a bounded work queue and settles them strictly in arrival order. The queue applies backpressure: once it is full, no further instruction is taken until settlement drains one. Submission rights are governed by a mandate generation number that the clearing house rotates from time to time; a member bank may only submit while it is accredited and while the mandate generation it holds matches the current one. Member banks can be slow without being failed, so a bank may sit on an out-of-date mandate generation for a while and then catch up.

The system behaves as follows. Submit appends an instruction to the tail of the queue, and requires that the submitting bank is currently accredited, that its mandate generation matches the clearing house's current generation, and that the queue is not already at capacity. SettleHead takes the instruction at the head of the queue, removes it, and advances the cleared-instruction counter, which saturates at its maximum rather than growing without bound. RotateMandate advances the clearing house's mandate generation, which instantly makes every bank that has not yet refreshed stale. Sync is the slow bank catching up: a bank whose mandate generation is behind adopts the current generation. Revoke withdraws a bank's accreditation and, in the same step, purges every instruction that bank has left waiting in the queue, so that nothing submitted by a bank that has lost its mandate can still be settled. Accredit admits a bank that is not currently accredited back into the membership without touching the queue.

The point of the design is that the queue is only ever allowed to contain work that a currently accredited member put there, even though accreditation can be withdrawn while instructions are already waiting.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every instruction waiting in the settlement queue was submitted by a bank that is still accredited.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the settlement queue is full, it eventually has room again.

---- MODULE W4Od16m1p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS RingSize, TotalUnits, MaxDraw

Stations == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Succ(i) == (i + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES token, vault, hands, dispensed

vars == <<token, vault, hands, dispensed>>

RECURSIVE HandTotal(_)
HandTotal(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN hands[x] + HandTotal(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Stations
    /\ vault \in 0 .. TotalUnits
    /\ hands \in [Stations -> 0 .. TotalUnits]
    /\ dispensed \in 0 .. TotalUnits

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ vault = TotalUnits
    /\ hands = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ dispensed = 0

Withdraw(n) ==
    /\ n <= vault
    /\ vault' = vault - n
    /\ hands' = [hands EXCEPT ![token] = hands[token] + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, dispensed>>

DispenseOne ==
    /\ hands[token] > 0
    /\ hands' = [hands EXCEPT ![token] = hands[token] - 1]
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, vault>>

ReturnOne ==
    /\ hands[token] > 0
    /\ hands' = [hands EXCEPT ![token] = hands[token] - 1]
    /\ vault' = vault + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, dispensed>>

PassToken ==
    /\ hands[token] = 0
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, hands, dispensed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxDraw : Withdraw(n)
    \/ DispenseOne
    \/ ReturnOne
    \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EveryUnitIsAccountedFor ==
    vault + HandTotal(Stations) + dispensed = TotalUnits
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    TotalUnits = 3
    MaxDraw = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT EveryUnitIsAccountedFor
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A pharmacy's controlled-substance dispenser is operated from several dispensing stations arranged in a ring. A single token circulates around the ring, and only the station currently holding the token may touch the vault. Every unit of the controlled drug is accounted for at all times: a unit is either sitting in the vault, in the hands of one of the stations, or already dispensed to a patient. Stations can be slow without being failed — a station may keep units in hand for as long as it likes before giving them back, and the ring simply waits, because the token cannot move on until the holder's hands are empty.

The system behaves as follows. Withdraw lets the station holding the token take some positive number of units out of the vault into its own hands, and requires the vault to actually contain that many. DispenseOne takes one unit out of the token holder's hands and gives it to a patient, incrementing the dispensed total; this is the only step that moves a unit out of the pharmacy's custody. ReturnOne puts one unit from the token holder's hands back into the vault. PassToken advances the token to the next station around the ring, and may only fire when the current holder's hands are empty, so a station must either dispense or return everything it withdrew before the ring can move on.

Because a unit in a station's hands is neither in the vault nor dispensed, the count of units in hand has to be part of the accounting; the design would be wrong if a withdrawal or a return ever adjusted only one side of the books.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units in the vault, the units held in the stations' hands, and the units already dispensed always add up to the pharmacy's total stock.

---- MODULE W4Od4m1p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS RingSize, MaxUses

Bays == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Succ(i) == (i + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES token, onPump, stage, uses

vars == <<token, onPump, stage, uses>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Bays
    /\ onPump \subseteq Bays
    /\ stage \in [Bays -> {"unprimed", "primed", "spent"}]
    /\ uses \in 0 .. MaxUses

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ onPump = {}
    /\ stage = [b \in Bays |-> "unprimed"]
    /\ uses = 0

Prime ==
    /\ stage[token] = "unprimed"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![token] = "primed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, onPump, uses>>

Draw ==
    /\ stage[token] = "primed"
    /\ onPump = {}
    /\ onPump' = {token}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, stage, uses>>

Release(b) ==
    /\ b \in onPump
    /\ onPump' = onPump \ {b}
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "spent"]
    /\ uses' = IF uses < MaxUses THEN uses + 1 ELSE uses
    /\ UNCHANGED token

PassToken ==
    /\ onPump = {}
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![token] = "unprimed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onPump, uses>>

ReleaseAny == \E b \in Bays : Release(b)

Next ==
    \/ Prime
    \/ Draw
    \/ ReleaseAny
    \/ PassToken

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(ReleaseAny)
    /\ WF_vars(PassToken)

OnlyTheTokenHolderDrawsFromThePump ==
    \A b \in onPump : token = b

TokenVisitsEveryBay ==
    \A b \in Bays : (token # b) ~> (token = b)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    MaxUses = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheTokenHolderDrawsFromThePump
PROPERTY TokenVisitsEveryBay
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash bays arranged in a ring, all fed by a single high-pressure pump. The pump is the critical resource: at most one bay may be drawing from it at any instant. Access is arbitrated by a token that circulates around the ring in a fixed order. A bay can be slow without being failed: after the token arrives it may take arbitrarily long to prime its nozzles before it actually draws from the pump, and the ring simply waits during that time.

The system behaves as follows. Prime is the slow step: the bay currently holding the token, if it has not yet primed or drawn this visit, primes its nozzles. Draw puts the token holder on the pump, and requires that the bay has primed and that nobody is currently on the pump. Release takes the bay off the pump and marks it as having had its turn this visit, and also advances the pump-use counter, which saturates at its maximum rather than growing without bound. PassToken hands the token to the next bay around the ring; it may fire only while nobody is on the pump, and in the same step it resets the bay it is leaving back to the unprimed state so that the bay starts fresh the next time the token comes around.

Notice that a bay which has already had its turn cannot prime again during the same visit, so a bay cannot monopolise the pump by cycling through draw and release while holding the token; once its turn is spent the only thing left to happen at that bay is for the token to move on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any bay drawing from the high-pressure pump is the bay that currently holds the ring token.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The token eventually reaches every bay on the ring.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Blocks, Fleet, Nominal, MaxOverrides

Authority == "authority"
MaxQueue == Nominal + MaxOverrides
Queues == UNION { [1 .. n -> {Authority}] : n \in 0 .. MaxQueue }

VARIABLES depot, queue, occupied, completed, overrides

vars == <<depot, queue, occupied, completed, overrides>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ depot \in 0 .. Fleet
    /\ queue \in Queues
    /\ occupied \subseteq Blocks
    /\ completed \in 0 .. Fleet
    /\ overrides \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ depot = Fleet
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ occupied = {}
    /\ completed = 0
    /\ overrides = MaxOverrides

Dispatch ==
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ Len(queue) < Nominal
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, Authority)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, completed, overrides>>

OverrideDispatch ==
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ Len(queue) >= Nominal
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ overrides > 0
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, Authority)
    /\ overrides' = overrides - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, completed>>

EnterBlock(b) ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ b \notin occupied
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, completed, overrides>>

LeaveBlock(b) ==
    /\ b \in occupied
    /\ occupied' = occupied \ {b}
    /\ completed' = completed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, queue, overrides>>

Recall(b) ==
    /\ b \in occupied
    /\ occupied' = occupied \ {b}
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, completed, overrides>>

Next ==
    \/ Dispatch
    \/ OverrideDispatch
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : EnterBlock(b) \/ LeaveBlock(b) \/ Recall(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EveryTrainIsSomewhere ==
    depot + Len(queue) + Cardinality(occupied) + completed = Fleet
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {k1, k2}
    Fleet = 3
    Nominal = 2
    MaxOverrides = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT EveryTrainIsSomewhere
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling block system moves trains from a depot, through a bounded dispatch queue of movement authorities, into track blocks, and finally out of the controlled territory. Every train is always in exactly one of those places, and the total number of trains in the system is fixed. The dispatch queue applies backpressure: normally no authority is issued once the queue is at its nominal capacity. A privileged controller override exists for degraded operation, and it is the only way an authority can be issued while the queue is already full; the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. Dispatch takes one train out of the depot and appends an authority for it to the dispatch queue, and requires both that the depot is not empty and that the queue is below its nominal capacity. OverrideDispatch is the privileged path: with the queue standing exactly at nominal capacity, a train still in the depot, and override budget remaining, the controller appends an authority anyway, pushing the queue past its nominal length and spending one unit of override budget. EnterBlock consumes the authority at the head of the queue and places that train into a track block that is currently clear. LeaveBlock moves a train out of an occupied block and out of the controlled territory, incrementing the count of trains that have completed their run. Recall moves a train out of an occupied block back into the depot instead, where it is available to be dispatched again.

Because a train sitting as an authority in the dispatch queue is neither in the depot nor on the track, the queue length is part of the train count; an override that appended an authority without taking the train out of the depot, or a block entry that failed to consume its authority, would show up immediately as a train appearing from nowhere.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The trains in the depot, the authorities waiting in the dispatch queue, the occupied track blocks, and the trains that have completed their run always add up to the fixed fleet size.

---- MODULE W4Od12m5p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members

Unassigned == "unassigned"

VARIABLES assigned, atStation, candidate, ballot, roster

vars == <<assigned, atStation, candidate, ballot, roster>>

Nominee == CHOOSE m \in candidate : TRUE
Threshold == Cardinality(roster) \div 2 + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ assigned \in Members \cup {Unassigned}
    /\ atStation \subseteq Members
    /\ candidate \subseteq Members
    /\ Cardinality(candidate) <= 1
    /\ ballot \subseteq Members
    /\ roster \subseteq Members

Init ==
    /\ assigned = Unassigned
    /\ atStation = {}
    /\ candidate = {}
    /\ ballot = {}
    /\ roster = Members

Nominate(m) ==
    /\ candidate = {}
    /\ assigned = Unassigned
    /\ m \in roster
    /\ candidate' = {m}
    /\ ballot' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, atStation, roster>>

CastVote(m) ==
    /\ candidate # {}
    /\ m \in roster
    /\ m \notin ballot
    /\ ballot' = ballot \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, atStation, candidate, roster>>

GrantAccess ==
    /\ candidate # {}
    /\ assigned = Unassigned
    /\ Cardinality(ballot) >= Threshold
    /\ assigned' = Nominee
    /\ candidate' = {}
    /\ ballot' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atStation, roster>>

EnterStation(m) ==
    /\ assigned = m
    /\ m \notin atStation
    /\ atStation' = atStation \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, candidate, ballot, roster>>

LeaveStation(m) ==
    /\ m \in atStation
    /\ atStation' = atStation \ {m}
    /\ assigned' = Unassigned
    /\ UNCHANGED <<candidate, ballot, roster>>

Relinquish ==
    /\ assigned # Unassigned
    /\ atStation = {}
    /\ assigned' = Unassigned
    /\ UNCHANGED <<atStation, candidate, ballot, roster>>

RosterChange(S) ==
    /\ S # {}
    /\ S # roster
    /\ roster' = S
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, atStation, candidate, ballot>>

LeaveAny == \E m \in Members : LeaveStation(m)

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members : Nominate(m) \/ CastVote(m) \/ EnterStation(m) \/ LeaveStation(m)
    \/ GrantAccess
    \/ Relinquish
    \/ \E S \in SUBSET Members : RosterChange(S)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(LeaveAny \/ Relinquish)

OnlyTheAssignedMemberStandsAtTheStation ==
    atStation \subseteq {assigned}

AssignmentsAreAlwaysGivenUp == (assigned # Unassigned) ~> (assigned = Unassigned)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Members = {m1, m2, m3}
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyTheAssignedMemberStandsAtTheStation
PROPERTY AssignmentsAreAlwaysGivenUp
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker has one cross-match workstation that lab members must not share: at most one member may be working at it at a time. Rather than a lock, the lab uses quorum voting. A member is nominated for the workstation, the members on the current duty roster vote, and a strict majority of the roster carries the nomination. The duty roster itself changes at runtime as shifts turn over, so the number of votes a nomination needs can go up or down while that nomination is still being voted on.

The system behaves as follows. Nominate opens a ballot when none is open and the workstation is unassigned, naming a member of the current roster as the candidate and clearing the vote set. CastVote records the support of one member who is on the current roster and has not yet voted in this ballot. GrantAccess closes a successful ballot: with a strict majority of the current roster's members having voted and the workstation still unassigned, the candidate becomes the assigned member, the ballot closes and the vote set clears. EnterStation puts the assigned member physically at the workstation. LeaveStation takes a member away from the workstation and, in the same step, gives up that member's assignment, so a member cannot step away and then step back in on the same grant. Relinquish covers the assigned member who never turned up: with nobody physically at the workstation, an outstanding assignment is simply given up. RosterChange replaces the duty roster with any non-empty set of members, which is how the majority threshold moves at runtime.

The scenario the design must exclude is a member standing at the workstation whose assignment has already gone away or was never granted, since that is exactly the case in which two members could end up cross-matching at once.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of members physically at the cross-match workstation never contains anyone other than the member currently assigned to it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: An assignment of the workstation is always eventually given up.

---- MODULE W4Od19m3p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Servers, Books, MaxTerm

NoLeader == "noleader"
Terms == 0 .. MaxTerm
Majority == Cardinality(Servers) \div 2 + 1

VARIABLES term, leaderOf, votes, ownTerm, reservations, crashed

vars == <<term, leaderOf, votes, ownTerm, reservations, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in Terms
    /\ leaderOf \in [Terms -> Servers \cup {NoLeader}]
    /\ votes \subseteq Servers
    /\ ownTerm \in [Servers -> Terms]
    /\ reservations \subseteq (Books \X Servers \X Terms)
    /\ crashed \subseteq Servers

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leaderOf = [t \in Terms |-> NoLeader]
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ ownTerm = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ reservations = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Campaign(s) ==
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ ownTerm' = [ownTerm EXCEPT ![s] = term + 1]
    /\ votes' = {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaderOf, reservations, crashed>>

Vote(s) ==
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ ownTerm[s] < term
    /\ ownTerm' = [ownTerm EXCEPT ![s] = term]
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderOf, reservations, crashed>>

BecomeLeader(s) ==
    /\ s \in votes
    /\ ownTerm[s] = term
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Majority
    /\ leaderOf[term] = NoLeader
    /\ leaderOf' = [leaderOf EXCEPT ![term] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, votes, ownTerm, reservations, crashed>>

Grant(s, bk) ==
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ leaderOf[term] = s
    /\ ownTerm[s] = term
    /\ <<bk, s, term>> \notin reservations
    /\ reservations' = reservations \cup {<<bk, s, term>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderOf, votes, ownTerm, crashed>>

Crash(s) ==
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderOf, votes, ownTerm, reservations>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Campaign(s) \/ Vote(s) \/ BecomeLeader(s) \/ Crash(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers, bk \in Books : Grant(s, bk)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReservationsCarryTheirTermsLeader ==
    \A e \in reservations : leaderOf[e[3]] = e[2]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Servers = {s1, s2, s3}
    Books = {bk1, bk2}
    MaxTerm = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ReservationsCarryTheirTermsLeader
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A library book reservation system is served by a cluster of branch servers, exactly one of which is the elected leader for the current term and the only one entitled to hand out reservations. Leadership changes by election with failover, and a server can crash silently: it stops taking part with no announcement at all, which is precisely why the term counter and the record of who led each term exist. Alongside those, the cluster keeps a reservation log, each entry naming the book, the server that granted it, and the term in force at the time.

The system behaves as follows. Campaign starts a new election: an uncrashed server bumps the term counter, adopts the new term as its own, and starts the vote set containing only itself. Vote lets an uncrashed server whose own term is behind adopt the current term and join the vote set for it. BecomeLeader records a winner: a server that is in the vote set, whose own term matches the current term, that has the support of a strict majority of the cluster, and where no leader has yet been recorded for this term, is written into the leadership record as the leader of that term. Grant issues a reservation: the uncrashed server recorded as leader of the current term, whose own term still matches, appends a log entry naming the book, itself, and the current term. Crash silently disables a server, after which it can no longer campaign, vote or grant, though everything it has already written stays in the log and in the leadership record.

Because the leadership record for a term is written once and the term counter only ever moves forward, a log entry that names a term should be traceable to precisely the server that led that term. A server that had fallen behind, or one whose leadership had already been superseded, granting a reservation under a term it no longer legitimately holds is the failure this design must exclude.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every reservation in the log was granted by the server recorded as the leader of the term that reservation carries.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m6p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Blocks, Controllers, MaxTTL

NoOne == "noone"

VARIABLES owner, ttl, proceeding, setBy, crashed

vars == <<owner, ttl, proceeding, setBy, crashed>>

Lapsed == {b \in Blocks : owner[b] # NoOne /\ ttl[b] = 0}

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Blocks -> Controllers \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ ttl \in [Blocks -> 0 .. MaxTTL]
    /\ proceeding \subseteq Blocks
    /\ setBy \in [Blocks -> Controllers \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ owner = [b \in Blocks |-> NoOne]
    /\ ttl = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ proceeding = {}
    /\ setBy = [b \in Blocks |-> NoOne]
    /\ crashed = {}

Acquire(c, b) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ owner[b] = NoOne
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![b] = MaxTTL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proceeding, setBy, crashed>>

SetProceed(c, b) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ owner[b] = c
    /\ ttl[b] > 0
    /\ b \notin proceeding
    /\ proceeding' = proceeding \cup {b}
    /\ setBy' = [setBy EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ttl, crashed>>

SetDanger(c, b) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ owner[b] = c
    /\ b \in proceeding
    /\ proceeding' = proceeding \ {b}
    /\ setBy' = [setBy EXCEPT ![b] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ttl, crashed>>

Tick ==
    /\ \E b \in Blocks : ttl[b] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [b \in Blocks |-> IF ttl[b] > 0 THEN ttl[b] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, proceeding, setBy, crashed>>

ExpireLeases ==
    /\ Lapsed # {}
    /\ owner' = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b \in Lapsed THEN NoOne ELSE owner[b]]
    /\ proceeding' = proceeding \ Lapsed
    /\ setBy' = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b \in Lapsed THEN NoOne ELSE setBy[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ttl, crashed>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ttl, proceeding, setBy>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks : Acquire(c, b) \/ SetProceed(c, b) \/ SetDanger(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)
    \/ Tick
    \/ ExpireLeases

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Tick)
    /\ WF_vars(ExpireLeases)

ProceedAspectsBelongToTheCurrentLeaseholder ==
    \A b \in proceeding : setBy[b] = owner[b]

ProceedAspectsAlwaysClear ==
    \A b \in Blocks : (b \in proceeding) ~> (b \notin proceeding)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {k1, k2}
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    MaxTTL = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ProceedAspectsBelongToTheCurrentLeaseholder
PROPERTY ProceedAspectsAlwaysClear
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling block system lets several interlocking controllers set the aspect of track blocks, but a controller must first take a lease on a block. Leases carry a countdown and are not renewable, because a controller can crash silently: it stops working with no notice, and a block whose signal was left showing proceed by a dead controller is exactly the hazard the countdown exists to clear. Whenever a lease runs out, the block is taken back and its signal is forced back to danger in the same step.

The system behaves as follows. Acquire gives an uncrashed controller the lease on a block that nobody currently holds, starting that block's countdown at its full value. SetProceed lets the uncrashed holder of an unexpired lease put its block's signal to proceed, recording itself as the controller that set that aspect. SetDanger lets the uncrashed holder of a block put the signal back to danger and clears the record of who set it. Tick advances the clock across the whole railway at once, decrementing every block countdown that is still above zero. ExpireLeases fires whenever at least one leased block has run its countdown to zero, and in one step it takes back every such block: the lease is dropped, the signal is forced back to danger, and the record of who set the aspect is cleared. Crash silently disables a controller, after which it can no longer acquire leases or move signals, though the blocks it already holds stay leased to it until their countdowns run out.

The failure to exclude is a block sitting at proceed on the authority of a controller that no longer holds it — a stale aspect, whether it went stale because the lease expired or because someone else took the block over.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every block showing a proceed aspect was set to it by the controller that currently holds that block's lease.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every block showing a proceed aspect eventually returns to danger.

---- MODULE W4Od16m5p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Prescriptions, Pharmacists

NoOne == "noone"
Majority == Cardinality(Pharmacists) \div 2 + 1

VARIABLES stage, approvals, filledBy, pulled, crashed

vars == <<stage, approvals, filledBy, pulled, crashed>>

FilledBy(p) == {r \in Prescriptions : filledBy[r] = p}

TypeOK ==
    /\ stage \in [Prescriptions -> {"open", "voting", "filled"}]
    /\ approvals \in [Prescriptions -> SUBSET Pharmacists]
    /\ filledBy \in [Prescriptions -> Pharmacists \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ pulled \in [Pharmacists -> SUBSET Prescriptions]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Pharmacists

Init ==
    /\ stage = [r \in Prescriptions |-> "open"]
    /\ approvals = [r \in Prescriptions |-> {}]
    /\ filledBy = [r \in Prescriptions |-> NoOne]
    /\ pulled = [p \in Pharmacists |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = {}

OpenBallot(r) ==
    /\ stage[r] = "open"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "voting"]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<filledBy, pulled, crashed>>

Approve(p, r) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ stage[r] = "voting"
    /\ p \notin approvals[r]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![r] = approvals[r] \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, filledBy, pulled, crashed>>

Fill(p, r) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ stage[r] = "voting"
    /\ Cardinality(approvals[r]) >= Majority
    /\ filledBy[r] = NoOne
    /\ filledBy' = [filledBy EXCEPT ![r] = p]
    /\ pulled' = [pulled EXCEPT ![p] = pulled[p] \cup {r}]
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "filled"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approvals, crashed>>

Void(r) ==
    /\ stage[r] = "voting"
    /\ filledBy[r] = NoOne
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![r] = "open"]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![r] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<filledBy, pulled, crashed>>

Crash(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, approvals, filledBy, pulled>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Prescriptions : OpenBallot(r) \/ Void(r)
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists, r \in Prescriptions : Approve(p, r) \/ Fill(p, r)
    \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : Crash(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PulledDrugsMatchTheSharedRecord ==
    \A p \in Pharmacists : pulled[p] \subseteq FilledBy(p)
====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser handles controlled prescriptions, where physically pulling the drug from the cabinet is irreversible: once a pharmacist has it in hand there is no putting it back on the shelf as if nothing happened. For that reason a prescription may only be pulled after a quorum of the pharmacy's pharmacists has approved it, and it may be pulled at most once. Pharmacists can crash silently — a pharmacist can stop responding without notice, mid-ballot, and the remaining staff have no way to tell.

The system behaves as follows. OpenBallot moves a prescription from the open state into the voting state with an empty approval set. Approve records the support of one uncrashed pharmacist for a prescription that is currently being voted on, and no pharmacist approves the same prescription twice. Fill is the irreversible act: an uncrashed pharmacist, faced with a prescription in the voting state that has collected at least a strict majority of approvals and that the record shows nobody has yet filled, writes itself into the record as that prescription's filler, adds the prescription to its own set of drugs pulled from the cabinet, and moves the prescription to the filled state. Void abandons a ballot that has not been filled, returning the prescription to the open state and clearing its approvals so that voting can start over. Crash silently disables a pharmacist, who can then neither approve nor fill anything, although any ballot it already voted in keeps its vote.

The disaster case is two pharmacists both walking away from the cabinet holding the same prescription's drug — which is what happens if a pharmacist's personal record of what it pulled can contain a prescription that the shared record attributes to someone else, or to nobody at all.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Everything a pharmacist has pulled from the cabinet is a prescription the shared record attributes to that same pharmacist.

---- MODULE W4Od1m8p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Runways, Controllers, Fleet

Nobody == "nobody"

VARIABLES stack, occupied, departed, airportLock, runwayLock, used

vars == <<stack, occupied, departed, airportLock, runwayLock, used>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ stack \in 0 .. Fleet
    /\ occupied \subseteq Runways
    /\ departed \in 0 .. Fleet
    /\ airportLock \in Controllers \cup {Nobody}
    /\ runwayLock \in [Runways -> Controllers \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ used \subseteq Runways

Init ==
    /\ stack = Fleet
    /\ occupied = {}
    /\ departed = 0
    /\ airportLock = Nobody
    /\ runwayLock = [r \in Runways |-> Nobody]
    /\ used = {}

AcquireAirport(c) ==
    /\ airportLock = Nobody
    /\ airportLock' = c
    /\ used' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, occupied, departed, runwayLock>>

AcquireRunway(c, r) ==
    /\ airportLock = c
    /\ runwayLock[r] = Nobody
    /\ r \notin used
    /\ runwayLock' = [runwayLock EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, occupied, departed, airportLock, used>>

MoveToRunway(c, r) ==
    /\ runwayLock[r] = c
    /\ r \notin occupied
    /\ stack > 0
    /\ stack' = stack - 1
    /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<departed, airportLock, runwayLock, used>>

Depart(c, r) ==
    /\ runwayLock[r] = c
    /\ r \in occupied
    /\ occupied' = occupied \ {r}
    /\ departed' = departed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, airportLock, runwayLock, used>>

ReleaseRunway(c, r) ==
    /\ runwayLock[r] = c
    /\ r \notin occupied
    /\ runwayLock' = [runwayLock EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
    /\ used' = used \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, occupied, departed, airportLock>>

ReleaseAirport(c) ==
    /\ airportLock = c
    /\ \A r \in Runways : runwayLock[r] # c
    /\ airportLock' = Nobody
    /\ used' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, occupied, departed, runwayLock>>

DepartAny == \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : Depart(c, r)
ReleaseRunwayAny == \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : ReleaseRunway(c, r)
ReleaseAirportAny == \E c \in Controllers : ReleaseAirport(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : AcquireAirport(c) \/ ReleaseAirport(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways :
           AcquireRunway(c, r) \/ MoveToRunway(c, r) \/ Depart(c, r) \/ ReleaseRunway(c, r)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(DepartAny \/ ReleaseRunwayAny \/ ReleaseAirportAny)

EveryAircraftIsAccountedFor ==
    stack + Cardinality(occupied) + departed = Fleet

AirportLockIsAlwaysGivenBack ==
    (airportLock # Nobody) ~> (airportLock = Nobody)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Runways = {rw1, rw2}
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    Fleet = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT EveryAircraftIsAccountedFor
PROPERTY AirportLockIsAlwaysGivenBack
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands departure slots to ground controllers using a two-level lock hierarchy: a controller must first take the single airport lock, and only then may it take the lock on an individual runway. Every aircraft in the fleet is accounted for at all times — it is either waiting in the holding stack, sitting on a runway, or already departed. Controllers can be slow without being failed: a controller may sit on the airport lock for as long as it likes, and the rest of the field simply waits.

The system behaves as follows. AcquireAirport gives a controller the airport lock when it is free, and starts that controller's session with an empty set of runways already used. AcquireRunway gives the controller holding the airport lock the lock on a free runway, provided that runway has not already been used and given back during this session. MoveToRunway takes one aircraft out of the holding stack and places it on an empty runway whose lock the controller holds. Depart sends the aircraft on a runway the controller holds on its way, emptying the runway and incrementing the departed count. ReleaseRunway gives back a runway lock the controller holds, but only when that runway is empty, and records the runway as used for the remainder of the session so it cannot be taken again before the airport lock changes hands. ReleaseAirport gives back the airport lock, and requires that the controller is holding no runway locks at all; the used-runway set is cleared for the next session.

Because an aircraft sitting on a runway has left the holding stack but has not departed, the runway occupancy is part of the accounting; a move that took an aircraft off the stack without putting it anywhere, or a departure that emptied a runway without counting the aircraft out, would break the books immediately.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The aircraft in the holding stack, the aircraft occupying runways, and the aircraft that have departed always add up to the fixed size of the fleet.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The airport lock, once taken, is always eventually given back.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Servers, NumBatches, MaxTerm, MaxCapacity

NoOne == "noone"
Batches == 1 .. NumBatches
Majority == Cardinality(Servers) \div 2 + 1

VARIABLES term, leader, votes, phase, wiredTotal, capacity

vars == <<term, leader, votes, phase, wiredTotal, capacity>>

RECURSIVE AmountOf(_)
AmountOf(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN x + AmountOf(S \ {x})

WiredSet == {b \in Batches : phase[b] = "wired"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Servers \cup {NoOne}
    /\ votes \subseteq Servers
    /\ phase \in [Batches -> {"pending", "wired"}]
    /\ wiredTotal \in 0 .. MaxCapacity
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxCapacity

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoOne
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ phase = [b \in Batches |-> "pending"]
    /\ wiredTotal = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxCapacity

Campaign(s) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = NoOne
    /\ votes' = {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, wiredTotal, capacity>>

Vote(s) ==
    /\ s \notin votes
    /\ votes # {}
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, phase, wiredTotal, capacity>>

TakeLeadership(s) ==
    /\ leader = NoOne
    /\ s \in votes
    /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Majority
    /\ leader' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, votes, phase, wiredTotal, capacity>>

Wire(b) ==
    /\ leader # NoOne
    /\ phase[b] = "pending"
    /\ wiredTotal + b <= capacity
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "wired"]
    /\ wiredTotal' = wiredTotal + b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, votes, capacity>>

Recapitalise(n) ==
    /\ n # capacity
    /\ capacity' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, votes, phase, wiredTotal>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Campaign(s) \/ Vote(s) \/ TakeLeadership(s)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Wire(b)
    \/ \E n \in 0 .. MaxCapacity : Recapitalise(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WiredTotalMatchesTheWiredBatches ==
    wiredTotal = AmountOf(WiredSet)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Servers = {s1, s2, s3}
    NumBatches = 3
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxCapacity = 6
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WiredTotalMatchesTheWiredBatches
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch runs on a small cluster of settlement servers with leader election and failover. Only an elected leader may wire a batch, and wiring is irreversible: the funds leave and there is no unwinding the transfer. Each batch is identified by a number that is also the amount it moves. The bank tracks the total value wired so far, and the settlement window's capacity — the total value the window will allow — is recapitalised at runtime by the treasury and may be raised or lowered at any moment.

The system behaves as follows. Campaign starts a fresh election: the term counter advances, the leadership for the new term is vacant, and the campaigning server is the sole initial member of the vote set. Vote adds a server to the vote set for the election currently under way. TakeLeadership makes a server that is in the vote set the leader, provided a strict majority of the cluster has voted and no leader has yet been established for this term. Wire is the irreversible act: with a leader established, a batch that is still pending is wired, provided the value already wired plus this batch's amount stays within the settlement window's capacity; the batch moves to the wired state and its amount is added to the running wired total. Recapitalise sets the settlement window's capacity to any new value, which may be below what has already been wired.

The books have to balance: the running wired total is the bank's authoritative statement of how much has left, and the set of batches marked wired is the authoritative statement of what left. A batch wired a second time would add its amount to the running total again without changing the set of wired batches, and the two statements would immediately disagree.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The running wired total always equals the sum of the amounts of exactly those batches marked as wired.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m1p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS RingSize, Chutes, MaxBags, MaxOverrides

Unset == -1
Stations == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Succ(i) == (i + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES token, programmedBy, inTransit, waiting, overrides

vars == <<token, programmedBy, inTransit, waiting, overrides>>

Blank == [c \in Chutes |-> Unset]

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Stations
    /\ programmedBy \in [Chutes -> Stations \cup {Unset}]
    /\ inTransit \subseteq Chutes
    /\ waiting \in 0 .. MaxBags
    /\ overrides \in 0 .. MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ programmedBy = Blank
    /\ inTransit = {}
    /\ waiting = MaxBags
    /\ overrides = MaxOverrides

SetRoute(c) ==
    /\ programmedBy[c] = Unset
    /\ programmedBy' = [programmedBy EXCEPT ![c] = token]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inTransit, waiting, overrides>>

ClearRoute(c) ==
    /\ programmedBy[c] = token
    /\ c \notin inTransit
    /\ programmedBy' = [programmedBy EXCEPT ![c] = Unset]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inTransit, waiting, overrides>>

RouteBag(c) ==
    /\ programmedBy[c] # Unset
    /\ c \notin inTransit
    /\ waiting > 0
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit \cup {c}
    /\ waiting' = waiting - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, programmedBy, overrides>>

DeliverBag(c) ==
    /\ c \in inTransit
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, programmedBy, waiting, overrides>>

PassToken ==
    /\ inTransit = {}
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ programmedBy' = Blank
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inTransit, waiting, overrides>>

AdminForce(s) ==
    /\ overrides > 0
    /\ inTransit = {}
    /\ s # token
    /\ token' = s
    /\ programmedBy' = Blank
    /\ overrides' = overrides - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inTransit, waiting>>

DeliverAny == \E c \in Chutes : DeliverBag(c)

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Chutes : SetRoute(c) \/ ClearRoute(c) \/ RouteBag(c) \/ DeliverBag(c)
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E s \in Stations : AdminForce(s)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(DeliverAny)
    /\ WF_vars(PassToken)

ProgrammedChutesBelongToTheTokenHolder ==
    \A c \in Chutes : (programmedBy[c] # Unset) => (programmedBy[c] = token)

TokenReachesEveryStation ==
    \A s \in Stations : (token # s) ~> (token = s)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Chutes = {ch1, ch2}
    MaxBags = 2
    MaxOverrides = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ProgrammedChutesBelongToTheTokenHolder
PROPERTY TokenReachesEveryStation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport baggage router has a number of sorting stations arranged in a ring, all writing to the same set of diverter chutes. A single token circulates around the ring and only the station holding the token may program a chute's destination; when the token moves on, every routing that station programmed is wiped, because a routing left behind by a station that no longer holds the token is a stale instruction that could send a bag to the wrong pier. A privileged duty-manager override exists that can hand the token directly to a chosen station out of ring order, and the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. SetRoute lets the station holding the token program an unprogrammed chute, recording itself as the station that programmed it. ClearRoute lets the token holder unprogram a chute it programmed. RouteBag sends one waiting bag down a programmed chute that has no bag on it already, decreasing the number of bags still waiting and putting that chute into the in-transit state. DeliverBag completes a bag's journey, taking the chute out of the in-transit state. PassToken hands the token to the next station around the ring and wipes every chute programming in the same step; it may only fire when no bag is in transit, so the router never re-programmes a chute out from underneath a moving bag. AdminForce is the privileged path: the duty manager hands the token directly to any other station, spending one unit of override budget, and this also wipes every chute programming and likewise requires that nothing is in transit.

The failure to exclude is a chute standing programmed on the authority of a station that no longer holds the token, whether the token moved on around the ring or was snatched away by the duty manager.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every programmed chute was programmed by the station that currently holds the ring token.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The token eventually reaches every sorting station on the ring.
