CONSTANTS Float, MaxEpoch, MaxLot

VARIABLES pool, book, matched, withdrawn, capacity, epoch

vars == <<pool, book, matched, withdrawn, capacity, epoch>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0 .. Float
    /\ book \in 0 .. Float
    /\ matched \in 0 .. Float
    /\ withdrawn \in 0 .. Float
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. Float
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ pool = Float
    /\ book = 0
    /\ matched = 0
    /\ withdrawn = 0
    /\ capacity = Float
    /\ epoch = 0

Submit(n) ==
    /\ n <= pool
    /\ book + n <= capacity
    /\ pool' = pool - n
    /\ book' = book + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<matched, withdrawn, capacity, epoch>>

Match(n) ==
    /\ n <= book
    /\ book' = book - n
    /\ matched' = matched + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, withdrawn, capacity, epoch>>

Withdraw(n) ==
    /\ n <= book
    /\ book' = book - n
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, matched, capacity, epoch>>

Reconfigure(n) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ n # capacity
    /\ capacity' = n
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, book, matched, withdrawn>>

TrimToCapacity ==
    /\ book > capacity
    /\ book' = book - 1
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, matched, capacity, epoch>>

Resubmit(n) ==
    /\ n <= withdrawn
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn - n
    /\ pool' = pool + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, matched, capacity, epoch>>

    \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxLot : Submit(n) \/ Match(n) \/ Withdraw(n) \/ Resubmit(n)
    \/ \E n \in 0 .. Float : Reconfigure(n)
    \/ TrimToCapacity

    pool + book + matched + withdrawn = Float

CONSTANTS
    Float = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxLot = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TheFloatIsNeverCreatedOrDestroyed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction on a single security. Every share of the auction's fixed float is always in exactly one of four places: not yet submitted, resting in the order book, matched into an opening trade, or withdrawn and sitting with the member firm. The book operates under epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the exchange bumps an auction epoch whenever it changes the book's capacity, which is the largest number of shares the book will hold, and the capacity can be raised or lowered at runtime, including to a value below what is already resting.

The system behaves as follows. Submit moves a quantity of shares from the not-yet-submitted pool into the order book, and requires both that the pool holds that many and that the book will still be within its current capacity afterwards. Match takes a quantity out of the book and into the matched total, which is where shares that cross in the opening print end up. Withdraw takes a quantity out of the book and into the withdrawn total, which is where a member's pulled interest sits. Reconfigure bumps the auction epoch and sets a new book capacity, which may be smaller than the quantity currently resting in the book. TrimToCapacity handles that case: while the book is above its current capacity, one share at a time is pushed out of the book into the withdrawn total until the book fits again. Resubmit takes a quantity out of the withdrawn total and puts it back into the not-yet-submitted pool so it can be entered again in a later epoch.

Every one of those steps moves shares between exactly two of the four places, and the float never changes; a reconfiguration that shrank the book by simply discarding the overflow, rather than moving it to the member's withdrawn total, would destroy shares outright.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shares not yet submitted, resting in the book, matched into the opening trade, and withdrawn always add up to the security's fixed float.

CONSTANTS Robots, Controllers, MaxClaims

Free == "free"

VARIABLES reg, claims, dock, stamp, fleetOf

vars == <<reg, claims, dock, stamp, fleetOf>>

Bump(n) == IF n < MaxClaims THEN n + 1 ELSE n

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in Robots \cup {Free}
    /\ claims \in 0 .. MaxClaims
    /\ dock \subseteq Robots
    /\ stamp \in [Robots -> 0 .. MaxClaims]
    /\ fleetOf \in [Robots -> Controllers]

Init ==
    /\ reg = Free
    /\ claims = 0
    /\ dock = {}
    /\ stamp = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ fleetOf = [r \in Robots |-> CHOOSE c \in Controllers : TRUE]

Claim(r) ==
    /\ reg = Free
    /\ reg' = r
    /\ claims' = Bump(claims)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, stamp, fleetOf>>

PlugIn(r) ==
    /\ reg = r
    /\ r \notin dock
    /\ dock' = dock \cup {r}
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![r] = claims]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, claims, fleetOf>>

Unplug(r) ==
    /\ reg = r
    /\ reg' = Free
    /\ dock' = dock \ {r}
    /\ claims' = Bump(claims)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, fleetOf>>

Recall(r) ==
    /\ r \in dock
    /\ dock' = dock \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, claims, stamp, fleetOf>>

Reassign(r, c) ==
    /\ fleetOf[r] # c
    /\ fleetOf' = [fleetOf EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, claims, dock, stamp>>

UnplugAny == \E r \in Robots : Unplug(r)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Claim(r) \/ PlugIn(r) \/ Unplug(r) \/ Recall(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, c \in Controllers : Reassign(r, c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(UnplugAny)

    \A r \in dock : stamp[r] = claims

RegisterIsAlwaysReleased == (reg # Free) ~> (reg = Free)

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    Controllers = {ctl1, ctl2}
    MaxClaims = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DockedRobotsCarryTheCurrentStamp
PROPERTY RegisterIsAlwaysReleased
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares one high-current docking arm, and no two robots may ever be plugged into it at the same time. Two independent fleet controllers draw from the same pool of robots — a robot belongs to one controller or the other, and robots are reassigned between the two controllers while the warehouse is running — but both controllers arbitrate for the arm through the same compare-and-swap register. Each successful swap into the register also advances a claim counter, and a robot stamps the counter value it saw when it plugged in.

The system behaves as follows. Claim is the compare-and-swap: a robot swaps itself into the register when the register reads free, and the claim counter advances by one, saturating at its maximum rather than growing without bound. PlugIn puts the robot named in the register into the dock and stamps it with the current claim counter value; a robot already in the dock does not plug in again. Unplug is the release: the robot named in the register clears the register back to free, takes itself out of the dock in the same step, and advances the claim counter again. Recall lets a controller pull its robot out of the dock without touching the register, which leaves the register claimed but the dock empty. Reassign moves a robot from one controller to the other, which changes nothing about the register, the dock or the stamps.

The stamp is the point: because every claim and every release advances the claim counter, a robot that is still in the dock from an earlier claim carries an out-of-date stamp. A second robot could only join it in the dock by plugging in under a later counter value, so the dock holding two robots and the dock holding a robot with a stale stamp are the same failure.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every robot in the dock is stamped with the current value of the claim counter.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A claimed compare-and-swap register is always eventually released back to free.

---- MODULE W4Od19m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Portals, Capacity, Headroom, MaxVersion, MaxRetries

NoBase == -1

VARIABLES active, version, base, intent, retries

vars == <<active, version, base, intent, retries>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ active \in 0 .. Capacity + Headroom
    /\ version \in 0 .. MaxVersion
    /\ base \in [Portals -> (0 .. MaxVersion) \cup {NoBase}]
    /\ intent \in [Portals -> {"idle", "add", "drop"}]
    /\ retries \in [Portals -> 0 .. MaxRetries]

Init ==
    /\ active = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ base = [p \in Portals |-> NoBase]
    /\ intent = [p \in Portals |-> "idle"]
    /\ retries = [p \in Portals |-> 0]

BeginAdd(p) ==
    /\ intent[p] = "idle"
    /\ active < Capacity
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![p] = "add"]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, version, retries>>

BeginDrop(p) ==
    /\ intent[p] = "idle"
    /\ active > 0
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![p] = "drop"]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, version, retries>>

CommitAdd(p) ==
    /\ intent[p] = "add"
    /\ base[p] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ active' = active + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![p] = NoBase]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

CommitDrop(p) ==
    /\ intent[p] = "drop"
    /\ base[p] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ active' = active - 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![p] = NoBase]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

Retry(p) ==
    /\ intent[p] # "idle"
    /\ base[p] # version
    /\ retries[p] < MaxRetries
    /\ IF intent[p] = "add" THEN active < Capacity ELSE active > 0
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![p] = retries[p] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, version, intent>>

Abandon(p) ==
    /\ intent[p] # "idle"
    /\ base[p] # version
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![p] = NoBase]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, version, retries>>

Next ==
    \E p \in Portals :
        \/ BeginAdd(p) \/ BeginDrop(p)
        \/ CommitAdd(p) \/ CommitDrop(p)
        \/ Retry(p) \/ Abandon(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ActiveReservationsStayWithinShelfCapacity == active <= Capacity
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Portals = {pa, pb}
    Capacity = 2
    Headroom = 2
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxRetries = 1
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ActiveReservationsStayWithinShelfCapacity
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A library book reservation system is fronted by two independent reservation portals that share one pool of loanable copies. Neither portal locks the pool; they use optimistic locking with retry instead. A portal reads the pool's version number together with the count of active reservations, decides what it wants to do, and only commits if the version it read is still the pool's version — and every commit advances the version. Because the version has a finite range in this model, commits stop once it is exhausted. The whole point of the version check is that a portal which validated the shelf capacity at read time can trust that check at commit time, so the commit itself does not re-examine the capacity.

The system behaves as follows. BeginAdd starts an add on an idle portal, but only after the portal has seen that the active-reservation count is below the shelf capacity; the portal records the version it read. BeginDrop starts a drop on an idle portal, provided there is at least one active reservation, and likewise records the version it read. CommitAdd applies an add when the recorded version still matches the pool's version: the active count goes up by one and the version advances. CommitDrop applies a drop under the same version match: the active count goes down by one and the version advances. Retry handles the conflict case: a portal whose recorded version no longer matches re-reads the pool, spending one unit of its retry allowance; the re-read takes in both the current version and the current active count, so a retry is only possible while the portal's intent is still viable — an add needs the count to still be below capacity, a drop needs at least one active reservation. Abandon lets a portal whose recorded version no longer matches simply give up and go idle.

The interesting failure is both portals reading the same below-capacity count, then both committing an add: that is exactly what the version match rules out, since whichever portal commits first advances the version and forces the other into retry or abandonment.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of active reservations never exceeds the shelf capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od0m9p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Surgeons, MaxSlot, MaxEpoch

Vacant == "vacant"
Slots == 1 .. MaxSlot

VARIABLES epoch, capacity, board, mine, booking

vars == <<epoch, capacity, board, mine, booking>>

Bookings == [sur : Surgeons, slot : Slots, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]
Live == CHOOSE b \in booking : TRUE

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ capacity \in 0 .. MaxSlot
    /\ board \in [Slots -> Surgeons \cup {Vacant}]
    /\ mine \in [Surgeons -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ booking \subseteq Bookings
    /\ Cardinality(booking) <= 1

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ capacity = MaxSlot
    /\ board = [sl \in Slots |-> Vacant]
    /\ mine = [s \in Surgeons |-> {}]
    /\ booking = {}

Request(s, sl) ==
    /\ booking = {}
    /\ board[sl] = Vacant
    /\ booking' = {[sur |-> s, slot |-> sl, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, board, mine>>

Confirm ==
    /\ booking # {}
    /\ Live.ep = epoch
    /\ board[Live.slot] = Vacant
    /\ Live.slot <= capacity
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![Live.slot] = Live.sur]
    /\ mine' = [mine EXCEPT ![Live.sur] = mine[Live.sur] \cup {Live.slot}]
    /\ booking' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>

DropStale ==
    /\ booking # {}
    /\ \/ Live.ep # epoch
       \/ board[Live.slot] # Vacant
       \/ Live.slot > capacity
    /\ booking' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, board, mine>>

Reconfigure(n) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ capacity' = n
    /\ board' = [sl \in Slots |-> IF sl > n THEN Vacant ELSE board[sl]]
    /\ mine' = [s \in Surgeons |-> {sl \in mine[s] : sl <= n}]
    /\ UNCHANGED booking

Release(s, sl) ==
    /\ board[sl] = s
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![sl] = Vacant]
    /\ mine' = [mine EXCEPT ![s] = mine[s] \ {sl}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, booking>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Surgeons, sl \in Slots : Request(s, sl) \/ Release(s, sl)
    \/ Confirm
    \/ DropStale
    \/ \E n \in 0 .. MaxSlot : Reconfigure(n)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Confirm \/ DropStale)

BoardAssignmentsAppearInTheSurgeonsList ==
    \A sl \in Slots : (board[sl] # Vacant) => (sl \in mine[board[sl]])

BookingsAreAlwaysResolved == (booking # {}) ~> (booking = {})
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Surgeons = {su1, su2}
    MaxSlot = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BoardAssignmentsAppearInTheSurgeonsList
PROPERTY BookingsAreAlwaysResolved
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler assigns surgeons to numbered theatre slots. The scheduler uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration: whenever the day's theatre list is rebuilt, a schedule epoch advances and the number of slots actually open that day is reset, so the theatre capacity changes at runtime and can shrink below the highest slot already assigned. Only one provisional booking is ever in flight at a time, and each provisional booking is stamped with the epoch in which it was raised. Alongside the theatre board, which records who is assigned to each slot, every surgeon keeps their own list of slots they believe they hold.

The system behaves as follows. Request raises a provisional booking when none is in flight, naming a surgeon and a slot the theatre board currently shows as free, and stamping the booking with the current schedule epoch. Confirm turns the in-flight booking into a real assignment, and requires that the booking's epoch stamp still matches the current epoch, that the slot is still free on the board, and that the slot is within the theatre capacity now open; the board records the surgeon and the surgeon's own list gains the slot. DropStale discards the in-flight booking in every other case — a stale epoch stamp, a slot that has been taken in the meantime, or a slot that a reconfiguration has put out of range. Reconfigure advances the schedule epoch and sets a new theatre capacity, and in the same step it clears the board and every surgeon's list of any slot that now falls outside the capacity. Release gives up an assigned slot, clearing it from the board and from the holding surgeon's own list together.

The failure this design must exclude is the same theatre slot ending up in two surgeons' hands, which is what happens whenever a surgeon's private list and the theatre board stop agreeing about who holds a slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot the theatre board shows as assigned appears in the personal list of exactly the surgeon the board names.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A provisional booking in flight is always eventually resolved.

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxLoad, MaxRated, MaxAlighted

NoSnap == -1

VARIABLES load, rated, snap, alighted, servicing

vars == <<load, rated, snap, alighted, servicing>>

Cleared == [c \in Controllers |-> NoSnap]

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in 0 .. MaxLoad
    /\ rated \in 0 .. MaxRated
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> (0 .. MaxLoad) \cup {NoSnap}]
    /\ alighted \in 0 .. MaxAlighted
    /\ servicing \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ load = 0
    /\ rated = MaxRated
    /\ snap = Cleared
    /\ alighted = 0
    /\ servicing = FALSE

Read(c) ==
    /\ ~servicing
    /\ snap[c] = NoSnap
    /\ load < rated
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = load]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, rated, alighted, servicing>>

CasBoard(c) ==
    /\ ~servicing
    /\ snap[c] # NoSnap
    /\ snap[c] = load
    /\ load' = load + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rated, alighted, servicing>>

CasFail(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoSnap
    /\ snap[c] # load
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, rated, alighted, servicing>>

Alight ==
    /\ load > 0
    /\ load' = load - 1
    /\ alighted' = IF alighted < MaxAlighted THEN alighted + 1 ELSE alighted
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rated, snap, servicing>>

EnterService ==
    /\ ~servicing
    /\ servicing' = TRUE
    /\ snap' = Cleared
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, rated, alighted>>

SetCapacity(n) ==
    /\ servicing
    /\ n # rated
    /\ n >= load
    /\ rated' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, snap, alighted, servicing>>

LeaveService ==
    /\ servicing
    /\ servicing' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, rated, snap, alighted>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Read(c) \/ CasBoard(c) \/ CasFail(c)
    \/ \E n \in 0 .. MaxRated : SetCapacity(n)
    \/ Alight
    \/ EnterService
    \/ LeaveService

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CarLoadStaysWithinTheRatedCapacity == load <= rated
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {fc1, fc2}
    MaxLoad = 4
    MaxRated = 2
    MaxAlighted = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CarLoadStaysWithinTheRatedCapacity
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper boards riders into one car under a strict load limit. Several floor controllers all try to board riders at once, and they coordinate through a compare-and-swap on the car's load register: a controller reads the current load, checks it against the rated capacity, and later swaps in the incremented value only if the load register still reads exactly what it read. Because the swap only succeeds when nothing has changed, the capacity check made at read time is still valid at swap time, and the swap deliberately does not re-check it. The rated capacity itself changes at runtime — building services lowers it for heavy-goods runs and raises it again afterwards — and that is done under a service mode that first invalidates every outstanding read.

The system behaves as follows. Read has an idle controller take a snapshot of the current load, and requires the car not to be in service mode and the load to be below the rated capacity at that moment. CasBoard is the swap: a controller holding a snapshot that still matches the load register boards its rider, raising the load by one and going back to idle; it is blocked while the car is in service mode. CasFail is the losing side of a race: a controller whose snapshot no longer matches the load register discards it and goes back to idle. Alight takes one rider out of the car, lowering the load and advancing the alighted tally, which saturates at its maximum. EnterService puts the car into service mode and discards every controller's snapshot in the same step. SetCapacity changes the rated capacity to a new value, and may only be done while the car is in service mode and only to a value that is not below the number of riders currently in the car, since lowering the rating cannot make riders vanish. LeaveService takes the car back out of service mode so boarding can resume.

The load limit has to hold across all of that: two controllers that both read the same below-capacity load must not both board, and a capacity that drops while a controller is holding a stale read must not let that read through.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The car's load never exceeds the currently rated capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od5m2p2t2 ----

CONSTANTS Instances, Shards, Population, MaxParty

VARIABLES pool, reserved, playing, round, votes

vars == <<pool, reserved, playing, round, votes>>

Rounds == [inst : Instances, size : 1 .. MaxParty]
Live == CHOOSE r \in round : TRUE

RECURSIVE Held(_)
Held(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN reserved[x] + Held(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0 .. Population
    /\ reserved \in [Instances -> 0 .. Population]
    /\ playing \in 0 .. Population
    /\ round \subseteq Rounds
    /\ Cardinality(round) <= 1
    /\ votes \subseteq Shards

Init ==
    /\ pool = Population
    /\ reserved = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ playing = 0
    /\ round = {}
    /\ votes = {}

OpenRound(i, n) ==
    /\ round = {}
    /\ n <= pool
    /\ pool' = pool - n
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![i] = reserved[i] + n]
    /\ round' = {[inst |-> i, size |-> n]}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED playing

Vote(sh) ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ sh \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {sh}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserved, playing, round>>

CommitRound ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ votes = Shards
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![Live.inst] = reserved[Live.inst] - Live.size]
    /\ playing' = playing + Live.size
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED pool

AbortRound(sh) ==
    /\ round # {}
    /\ sh \notin votes
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![Live.inst] = reserved[Live.inst] - Live.size]
    /\ pool' = pool + Live.size
    /\ round' = {}
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED playing

Disband(n) ==
    /\ n <= playing
    /\ playing' = playing - n
    /\ pool' = pool + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, round, votes>>

VoteSome == \E sh \in Shards : Vote(sh)

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, n \in 1 .. MaxParty : OpenRound(i, n)
    \/ \E sh \in Shards : Vote(sh) \/ AbortRound(sh)
    \/ CommitRound
    \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxParty : Disband(n)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(VoteSome)
    /\ WF_vars(CommitRound)

EveryPlayerIsCountedExactlyOnce ==
    pool + Held(Instances) + playing = Population

RoundsInFlightAlwaysClose == (round # {}) ~> (round = {})

CONSTANTS
    Instances = {mm1, mm2}
    Shards = {sh1, sh2}
    Population = 3
    MaxParty = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT EveryPlayerIsCountedExactlyOnce
PROPERTY RoundsInFlightAlwaysClose
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker is run by two independent matchmaking instances that draw from one shared pool of waiting players. Every player is always in exactly one of three places: waiting in the shared pool, reserved by one of the two instances for a match it is trying to form, or already playing in a formed match. Forming a match is a two-phase commit across the region shards, and the shared pool has a single commit gate, so only one match-forming round is ever in flight; the two instances contend for that gate.

The system behaves as follows. OpenRound starts a round when the gate is free: an instance takes some number of players out of the shared pool and into its own reserved count, records the round with its own name and that party size, and starts the round with an empty vote set. Vote records one region shard's agreement with the round in flight. CommitRound closes a round that every region shard has agreed to: the reserved players of the round's instance move into the playing count and the gate is released. AbortRound closes a round that a region shard refuses before voting: the round's reserved players go straight back into the shared pool, the vote set clears, and the gate is released. Disband ends matches: a number of players who are playing return to the shared pool.

Note that a player reserved by an instance is out of the pool but not yet playing, so the reservation counts are as much a part of the census as the pool itself; a commit that moved players into the playing count without drawing down the reservation, or an abort that released the gate without giving the players back, would invent or lose players outright.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The players waiting in the shared pool, the players reserved by each instance, and the players in formed matches always add up to the fixed population of the lobby.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A match-forming round in flight is always eventually closed.
